events.promise: Plausible can turn trial signup completion into a conversion goal and show which sources and entry pages contributed to those signups.
events.arc: Introduce Plausible through one useful task, explain the smallest appropriate setup choice, show what becomes visible after a conversion, and send the reader to the official setup guide.

emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the official guide and determine whether their signup should be tracked with a pageview goal or a custom event goal.
emails.single_idea: Define trial signup completion as a Plausible goal, then use the goal-filtered dashboard to see which referrer sources and entry pages produced those conversions.
emails.objection: The reader may be unsure whether their signup flow needs code to track.
must_not_say: Do not presume which analytics tool, if any, the reader currently uses.
Do not presume the reader's traffic volume, conversion rate, privacy compliance status or technical stack.
Do not claim that Plausible will increase signups, improve conversion rates or reproduce Plausible's own measured results.
Do not use Plausible's 84% signup increase as proof that goal tracking caused a lift.
Do not imply that every signup flow can use a no-code pageview goal; custom event goals require a code snippet or script.
Do not expand into pricing, migration, funnels, trial-to-paid benchmarks, privacy compliance, uptime or the broader feature set.
emails.felt_need: Free-trial signups do not convert to paid at a rate the owner considers acceptable, even after a signup surge.
emails.status_quo: They add free trials that require a payment method upfront to try to convert website visitors into paying customers.
emails.mechanism: If signup completion reaches a distinct confirmation page, the reader can set that page as a pageview goal without changing code; if it does not, the guide explains the custom-event route. emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the signup should be configured as a pageview goal or a custom event goal.
emails.next_step_value: The guide explains the two goal types and how to set up and measure a conversion goal.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the guide does not configure the reader's site, record a conversion or establish that tracking will improve signup performance.

events.body:
Turn trial signup completion into a goal and see where those signups came from. Plausible Analytics is a privacy-friendly web analytics tool that shows website traffic and signup conversions in one dashboard.

If signup ends on a distinct confirmation page, set that page as a pageview goal with no code changes. If there is no distinct page, use a custom event goal, which requires a code snippet or script.

After the first conversion is recorded, the goal appears in the Goals section. Filter the dashboard by that goal to review conversion rate, referrer sources, entry pages and the pages where visitors converted.

Inspect the official goal-conversions guide to decide whether your signup should use a pageview goal or a custom event goal.

events.body:
If your SaaS offers a trial, which referrers and landing pages produce completed signups—not simply visits?

Plausible Analytics is a privacy-friendly web analytics tool that shows website traffic and signup conversions in one dashboard. Define signup completion as a goal, then compare conversion rates, referrer sources, entry pages and top converting pages.

Plausible has two core goal types. If signup ends on a distinct confirmation page, that page can become a pageview goal with no code changes. If there is no separate confirmation page, a custom event goal requires a code snippet or script.

The official goal-conversions guide explains both routes, so you can check your signup flow and choose the appropriate goal before configuring it.
